==Brazil==
[[Brazil|The country]] has 258 million subscribers in total, or a 125.7% penetration rate.<ref name="teleco1">{{cite web |title=Market Share das Operadoras |url=https://www.teleco.com.br/mshare.asp |access-date=2024-05-25 |website=Teleco |language=pt}}</ref> (Q1 2024)

[[Anatel]] regulates the country's [[telecommunications]].

Technologies like [[Advanced Mobile Phone System|AMPS]], [[D-AMPS|TDMA]], [[iDEN]] and [[CDMA]] 1x/EV-DO were used in the past by some of those networks and have been phased out in favor of newer systems.

On 20 April 2022, [[Oi (telecommunications)|Oi]]’s mobile network operations were sold to the country's three largest carriers, [[Vivo (telecommunications company)|Vivo]], [[Claro Brasil|Claro]] and [[TIM Brasil|TIM]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Financial Post |date=20 April 2022 |url=https://financialpost.com/pmn/business-pmn/purchase-of-brazils-oi-mobile-operations-is-concluded-says-tim |access-date=19 Jun 2022}}</ref> Over the following twelve months, customers were migrated to one of the other three carriers based on their area codes.

==Canada==
{{main|List of Canadian mobile phone companies}}

The country's telecom regulator is the [[Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission]] (CRTC). However, it does not regulate most aspects of mobile phone service; prices and service quality are not regulated at all, while spectrum allocation is handled by [[Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada]].

There are numerous [[mobile virtual network operator]]s, such as [[Virgin Mobile Canada]]. These are not presently listed due to difficulty retrieving data for all such operators, and uncertainty as to whether the figures below include MVNOs operating on the applicable networks.<ref>The Canadian Wireless Telecommunications Association only lists these five providers in its [http://www.cwta.ca/CWTASite/english/facts_figures_downloads/SubscribersStats_en_2007_Q3.pdf subscriber statistics].</ref>

==Costa Rica==
The country has 7.1 million subscribers in total;<ref name="auto">{{cite book |author=Superintendencia de Telecomunicaciones (SUTEL)|year=2015 |title=Estadísticas del sector de telecomunicaciones. Informe 2014. Costa Rica. |url=https://sutel.go.cr/sites/default/files/estadisticastelecomsutel2014baja_0.pdf |format=Online text reproduction |location=San Jose, Costa Rica|publisher=SUTEL |issn=2215-3683}}</ref> with 4.76 million people there are about 149 mobile lines for every 100 citizens (149%  penetration rate).

Until 2011, [[Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad]] had a monopoly on wireless communications. In November 2011, after the market was open as required by [[DR-CAFTA]], Claro and Movistar started service.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nacion.com/2011-11-08/ElPais/Movistar-abre-hoy-con-ofertas-para-competir-en-pospago.aspx |title=Movistar abre hoy con ofertas para competir en pospago - EL PAÍS - la Nación |access-date=13 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111110234000/http://www.nacion.com/2011-11-08/ElPais/Movistar-abre-hoy-con-ofertas-para-competir-en-pospago.aspx |archive-date=10 November 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nacion.com/2011-11-11/ElPais/Claro-se--estrena-con---ofertas-en-llamadas-al-Istmo-y-EE--UU.aspx |title=Claro se estrena con ofertas en llamadas al Istmo y EE. UU. - EL PAÍS - la Nación |access-date=13 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111113131540/http://www.nacion.com/2011-11-11/ElPais/Claro-se--estrena-con---ofertas-en-llamadas-al-Istmo-y-EE--UU.aspx |archive-date=13 November 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

The country's telecom regulator is SUTEL (Spanish)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sutel.go.cr|title=Sutel|work=sutel.go.cr}}</ref>

==Puerto Rico and United States Virgin Islands==
These U.S. territories have 3 million subscribers in total, or an 84% penetration rate.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.jrtpr.gobierno.pr/download/Junio%202012%20Publicacion.pdf |title=Líneas Alámbricas e Inalámbricas (Celulares) Diciembre 2001 - Junio 2012 |access-date=12 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131217224730/http://www.jrtpr.gobierno.pr/download/Junio%202012%20Publicacion.pdf |archive-date=17 December 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> (June 2012).

The telecom regulator for Puerto Rico and the United States Virgin Islands at federal level is the United States' Federal Communications Commission (FCC).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcc.gov/|title=Home|publisher=Federal Communications Commission}}</ref>

The local telecom regulator for Puerto Rico is the Junta Reglamentadora de Telecomunicaciones de Puerto Rico (JRTPR)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.jrtpr.gobierno.pr/ |title=Home |website=jrtpr.gobierno.pr}}</ref> The local telecom regulator for USVI is the USVI Public Services Commission (USVIPSC)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://psc.vi.gov/ |title=Building Bridges |publisher=Public Services Commission |date=2020-06-20 |access-date=2022-04-19}}</ref>

==United States==
{{main|List of mobile network operators in the United States|List of mobile virtual network operators in the United States}}

Mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs) in the United States lease wireless telephone and data service from Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) such as AT&T Mobility, T-Mobile US, or Verizon.

The country's telecom regulator is the [[United States Federal Communications Commission]].
